events.credibility_reason: Single-source claim: no human has read the proof or checked that the Lean statement matches the bullet. The witness is non-explicit and its degree is unstated. Epoch's public results do not list the run the README names. The repository itself was machine-written. No specific error has been identified, and the author is an established Epoch engineer, so it is not set aside.
events.ai_basis: found autonomously by a pre-release version of GPT-6 Astra (OpenAI)

events.credibility_reason: Claims a 'comprehensive' solution to a landmark problem with no stated scope. In about four years there has been no engagement and no publication. Later work (Jatar and Ng 2026, Tang 2025) still calls the problem open and does not cite it. arXiv flags substantial text overlap with another paper by the same authors.
The author withdrew it, citing an error on page 10.
Borcea (2003) gives concrete counterexamples to the main claims of all eight versions, and nobody has answered them.
No source in the record supports the attribution or the bound; it comes from a search summary only.

why: The statement asks one universal question at constant 1. A valid counterexample therefore answers all of it, so the Adamczewski/GPT-6 Astra disproof is scope whole. It is unreviewed: the only check is a Lean/Comparator build (F7), and the witness is non-explicit, so it is not checkable. I rated it doubtful rather than not_credible. No error has been identified and the author is an established figure, but the evidence is single-source, the Epoch run is unconfirmed, nobody has checked statement fidelity, and the repository was machine-written. The README says the witness was found autonomously by GPT-6 Astra, so its AI role is generated. Jatar and Ng's Schlicht asymptotic result is a restricted case, and that call was close: it is asymptotic rather than exact. AlphaEvolve's negative search delivered nothing, and its own quote shows only that it reproduced a known bound, so it is none. Dual, Blaschke, C*-algebra, Tischler-strong-form and constant-2 odd-polynomial results are variants. Constant bounds (Smale's 4, Crane, Conte et al., Beardon et al.) are bounds on the constant and leave the question open. Pre-window claimed proofs are knocked_down (Wang withdrawn; Schmieder refuted by Borcea), and Ma and Ma's is not_credible. Dubinin 2024 is year-only, so its after_snapshot is null.
doubts: The disproof's correctness rests entirely on an unreviewed machine-generated Lean development. Nobody has independently checked that Challenge.lean encodes the bullet: the unused K binder and the x/0 convention were judged harmless only by the researcher. The relation between the witness and Jatar and Ng's Schlicht result is unresolved. Marinov and Sendov's journal verification is treated as digested from secondary reports only.
